q.s: At which Harappan site was a terracotta model of a toy plough found?
q.x: A terracotta toy plough comes from Banawali (Haryana); the actual ploughed field was found at Kalibangan.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan site–find pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ropar – Dog buried with a human
q.x: The dockyard belongs to Lothal; Surkotada is known for doubtful horse bones.

q.s: The weights used in Dilmun (modern Bahrain region) followed the standard of:
q.x: Dilmun weights followed the Harappan standard, showing close trade links with the Indus people.

q.s: The Late Harappan (post-urban) phase is broadly dated to:
q.x: The Late Harappan phase ran c. 1900-1300 BCE, when people lived mainly in villages after the cities declined.

q.s: The theory that the Indus cities were destroyed by an Aryan invasion was put forward by:
q.x: Mortimer Wheeler used the Mohenjodaro skeletons and Indra 'Purandara' (fort-breaker) to argue for an Aryan massacre; the theory is now rejected.

q.s: The Kashikhandam, which refers to the sea trade of the Reddy kingdom, was written by:
q.x: Srinatha, court poet of the Reddis, wrote the Kashikhandam.

q.s: The treatise on architecture 'Samarangana Sutradhara' is attributed to:
q.x: Samarangana Sutradhara is attributed to King Bhoja of the Paramaras; Nitivakyamrita is Somadeva Suri's.

q.s: Which of the following Veda–priest pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The Atharvaveda was associated with the Brahman priest, who supervised the sacrifice.

q.s: The Mahasanghika sect of Buddhism is said to have originated at:
q.x: The Mahasanghika sect was born at Dhanyakataka (Amaravati); the Andhakas also took part in the Third Council as the Kathavatthu shows.

q.s: Buddhist monasteries like Amaravati were built close to towns mainly because:
o: Monks depended on daily alms from townspeople
q.x: Monks lived on daily alms and had to reach the town on the alms round; town merchants were also major donors.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the decline of Jainism?
o: Use of Sanskrit as its only language
q.x: Jainism declined due to lack of missionary zeal, loss of royal patronage, sectarian splits and severe austerity; it used Prakrit and regional languages widely.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the Mauryan judicial system was marked by:
o: A detailed written code of law
The absence of a written code of law
q.x: Megasthenes says the Mauryas had no written code of law; justice depended on memory and custom.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: In the Mauryan judicial ladder, the Sangrahana court stood just above the village court.
Megasthenes says the Mauryas had a detailed written code of law.
The parivrajika was a stationary (samstha) spy.
The Arthashastra makes no mention of spies.
q.x: The Sangrahana court was above the village court; Megasthenes says there was no written law and the parivrajika was a wandering spy.

q.s: In the Mauryan administration, the Akaradhyaksha was the superintendent of:
q.x: Akaradhyaksha was in charge of mines; Lakshanadhyaksha of the mint and Sunadhyaksha of the slaughterhouse.

q.s: Which of the following Mauryan superintendents is NOT correctly matched with his charge?
q.x: The Akshapataladhyaksha was the accountant-general; agriculture was under the Sitadhyaksha.

q.s: The southern Mauryan province of Dakshinapatha had its capital at:
q.x: Suvarnagiri was the capital of Dakshinapatha; Tosali was the capital of Kalinga, Ujjain of Avantipatha and Taxila of Uttarapatha.

q.s: Which of the following Mauryan province–capital pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: Dakshinapatha was governed from Suvarnagiri; Pataliputra was the imperial capital.

q.s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar, recording the conquests of Chandragupta II, stands in the courtyard of:
q.x: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar stands in the yard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following inscriptions does NOT belong to the Gupta rulers?
q.x: The Aihole inscription is of the Chalukya Pulakesin II.

q.s: The Haraha inscription records the victories of which Maukhari ruler?
q.x: The Haraha inscription records Ishanavarman's victories, including over the Andhras (Vishnukundins); the Asirgarh seal is of Sarvavarman.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'trivarga' of Hindu thought?
q.x: Dharma, artha and kama form the trivarga; moksha is the fourth purushartha.

q.s: Alauddin Khalji introduced market control mainly to:
o: Maintain a large army on low salaries
Help the peasants of the Doab
q.x: Price control kept prices low so a large standing army against the Mongols could live on fixed, low pay.

q.s: Tughlaqabad, the third city of Delhi, was built by:
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad; Jahanpanah, the fourth city, was built by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, 'Khalisa' land referred to:
o: Crown land whose revenue went to the royal treasury
q.x: Khalisa was crown land; iqta was revenue assigned to officials in place of salary and inam was religious grant land.

q.s: Token currency of copper and brass at par with silver was introduced by:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued token currency (1329-30); the Bahloli was the copper coin of Bahlol Lodi.

q.s: Which of the following coin–ruler pairs of the Delhi Sultanate is NOT correct?
q.x: The gold dinar became popular under Alauddin Khalji after the South Indian loot; the Bahloli was Bahlol Lodi's copper coin.

q.s: The Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and the Fatawa-i-Jahandari were written by:
q.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote both; the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi covers Balban to early Firoz.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Amir Khusrau?
q.x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is Barani's work on political theory.

q.s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), each revenue circle was expected to yield one crore of:
q.x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, the Mughal copper coin; the officers in charge were called karoris.

q.s: Aurangzeb was buried in a simple grave at:
q.x: Aurangzeb was buried at Khuldabad near Aurangabad; he died at Ahmadnagar in 1707.

q.s: During 1689-1700 the Maratha ruler Rajaram resisted the Mughals from the fort of:
q.x: Rajaram held out from Jinji; after his death in 1700 Tarabai led the war as regent for Shivaji II.

q.s: Charles II leased Bombay to the English East India Company in 1668 for an annual rent of:
q.x: Bombay was leased to the Company in 1668 for 10 pounds a year; it replaced Surat as the chief western settlement in 1687.

q.s: Uda Devi, a woman fighter of the Revolt of 1857, fought at:
q.x: Uda Devi fought at Sikandar Bagh, Lucknow; Azizun was at Kanpur and Jhalkari Bai at Jhansi.

q.s: Which of the following women is NOT associated with the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh was a 20th-century freedom fighter and Constituent Assembly member; the others fought in 1857.

q.s: Which commission reorganised the Indian army after the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: The Peel Commission (1859) reorganised the army: European troops were increased and artillery kept in European hands.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The European to Indian troop ratio in the Bengal Army was fixed at 1:5.
Recruitment shifted towards Awadh and Bihar after 1857.
The Peel Commission was appointed in 1872.
After 1857 the artillery was kept in European hands.
q.x: Artillery stayed European; the Peel Commission (1859) fixed 1:2 in Bengal and recruitment moved to Punjab, Nepal and NWFP.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act 1858, the Secretary of State for India was assisted by:
q.x: The 1858 Act abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors; the Secretary of State was advised by a 15-member Council of India.

q.s: Bahadur Shah II, proclaimed Emperor by the rebels of 1857, died in exile at:
q.x: Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.

q.s: In the Battle of Wandiwash (1760), the English forces were commanded by:
q.x: Eyre Coote defeated Lally at Wandiwash on 22 January 1760; Bussy was taken prisoner.

q.s: Who described Robert Clive as a 'heaven-born general'?
q.x: William Pitt the Elder called Clive a 'heaven-born general'.

q.s: Which of the following came to be called the 'Magna Carta' of the English East India Company?
q.x: The Farman of 1717 issued by Farrukhsiyar gave the Company duty-free trade in Bengal on dastaks and is called its Magna Carta.

q.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal, 'Nizamat' referred to:
q.x: Nizamat covered police, criminal justice and law and order, left with the Nawab; Diwani (revenue and civil justice) went to the Company.

q.s: After abolishing the Dual Government, Warren Hastings shifted the treasury:
q.x: Hastings moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta.

q.s: The Company's request for a government loan in 1772 was followed by the passing of:
q.x: Its financial crisis and the loan request led to the Regulating Act of 1773.

q.s: The universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were established in 1857 during the tenure of:
q.x: Lord Canning, the last Governor-General under the Company and first Viceroy, saw the three universities founded in 1857.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT take place during the tenure of Lord Canning?
o: Founding of the universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
q.x: The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) belongs to Lord Ripon's time.

q.s: The Governor-General of Bengal was made the Governor-General of India by the:
q.x: The Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India with exclusive law-making power, the final step in centralisation.

q.s: The Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company (1854) is associated with:
q.x: Cowasji Nanabhai Davar founded the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company in 1854.

q.s: The Indian Famine Code of 1883 was based on the report of which Famine Commission?
q.x: The Strachey Commission (1878-80), set up after the Great Famine of 1876-78, led to the Famine Code; Lyall (1897) and MacDonnell (1900) came later.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Famine Commission of British India?
q.x: The Hunter Commission (1882) dealt with education; Strachey (1880), Lyall (1898) and MacDonnell (1901) were Famine Commissions.

q.s: The Godavari anicut was built by Arthur Cotton at:
q.x: The Godavari anicut is at Dowleswaram; the Krishna anicut is at Bezwada and the K.C. Canal begins at Sunkesula.

q.s: Who became the first Indian President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925?
q.x: The Swarajist Vithalbhai Patel was elected in August 1925; Frederick Whyte was the first President.

q.s: The Self-Respect Movement was started in Tamil Nadu by:
q.x: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar) began the Self-Respect Movement in 1925; Sree Narayana Guru's SNDP was in Kerala.

q.s: The Shuddhi movement, which aimed at reconversion to Hinduism, was associated with:
q.x: Shuddhi was an Arya Samaj movement; its aggressive 1920s campaign was led by Swami Shraddhanand.

q.s: The Faraizi Movement in Bengal was founded by:
q.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement; his son Dudu Miyan carried it on.

q.s: The East India Association was founded at London in 1866 by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London (1866).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a founder of the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870)?
q.x: The Sabha was founded by Ranade, G.V. Joshi and S.H. Chiplunkar; Tilak was not among its founders.

q.s: Who was the first Indian member of the Welby Commission (1895) on Indian expenditure?
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji sat on the Welby Commission; Gokhale only gave evidence before it.

q.s: Gandhi formed the Satyagraha Sabha against the Rowlatt Act in February 1919 at:
q.x: The Satyagraha Sabha was formed at Bombay on 24 February 1919.

q.s: At the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the Lt. Governor of Punjab was:
q.x: Michael O'Dwyer was the Lt. Governor; General Dyer ordered the firing.

q.s: Who among the following acted as mediators between Gandhi and Irwin before the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
Madan Mohan Malaviya and Rajendra Prasad
q.x: Sapru and Jayakar mediated; the pact was signed at Delhi on 5 March 1931.

q.s: INA Day, as part of the campaign for the INA accused, was observed on:
q.x: INA Day was observed on 12 November 1945; police fired on Calcutta students on 21 November 1945.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam's autobiography is titled:
q.x: Prakasam's autobiography is Naa Jeevita Yatra; its fourth part was written by Tenneti Viswanatham.

q.s: Which of the following newspapers was NOT started by B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: Al-Hilal was Abul Kalam Azad's Urdu weekly; Mook Nayak, Bahishkrit Bharat and Janata were Ambedkar's.

q.s: The revolutionary paper 'Yugantar' was associated with:
q.x: Yugantar was brought out by Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendra Nath Dutt; Swadeshabhimani was Ramakrishna Pillai's.

q.s: Privy purses of the former princes were abolished by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 26th Amendment (1971) abolished privy purses; the 7th (1956) ended Part B states and the office of Rajpramukh.

q.s: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission with effect from:
q.x: NITI Aayog came into being on 1 January 2015; Montek Singh Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

q.s: The Rajiv Aarogyasri health insurance scheme was launched in Andhra Pradesh under Chief Minister:
q.x: Rajiv Aarogyasri (2007) and Indiramma housing came under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy; Janmabhoomi under Chandrababu Naidu.

q.s: The first secretary of the Andhra Congress Circle (formed in 1918) was:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya was its first secretary; the Circle was sanctioned at the Calcutta session of 1917.

q.s: The AICC meeting of 1921, associated with the Tilak Swaraj Fund, was held at:
q.x: The AICC met at Bezawada in 1921 and resolved to raise the Tilak Swaraj Fund.

q.s: Which of the following States was NOT formed primarily on a linguistic basis?
q.x: Uttarakhand was created in 2000 on grounds of regional backwardness and administration; Andhra, Gujarat and Maharashtra were linguistic states.

q.s: Inamgaon, a well-known Chalcolithic village site, belongs to which culture?
q.x: Inamgaon is a Jorwe culture site in the Pravara-Godavari zone; Jorwe is dated c. 1400-700 BCE.

q.s: The Chalcolithic site of Navdatoli on the Narmada was excavated by:
q.x: Navdatoli was excavated by H.D. Sankalia.

q.s: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I is significant as the first long inscription in:
q.x: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription is the first long Sanskrit inscription; it records the repair of the Sudarshana lake without forced labour or new taxes.

q.s: Which Purana is considered a main source for the genealogy of the Satavahanas?
q.x: The Matsya Purana is a main source of Satavahana genealogy; the Vayu and Vishnu Puranas mention 17 kings and 272 years.

q.s: Under the Ikshvakus, Buddhism in Andhra was patronised mainly by:
q.x: Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices while their queens patronised Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: The Ikshvaku period marks a shift from the Satavahana trade economy to:
q.x: The Ikshvaku age moved towards an agrarian, agrahara-based order, with revenue spent on tanks and canals.

q.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II was composed by:
q.x: Ravikirti composed the Aihole inscription and claimed fame like Kalidasa and Bharavi.

q.s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the banks of the:
q.x: The Aihole inscription records Harsha's defeat on the Narmada.

q.s: The temples of the Vengi school of the Eastern Chalukyas were mainly built of:
q.x: Vengi school temples used local sandstone on a raised jagati in the Vesara (Chalukya) idiom, leading into the Chalukya-Chola style.

q.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler bore the title 'Vishamasiddhi'?
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, founder of the Vengi line, was called Vishamasiddhi; Narendramrigaraja was Vijayaditya II.

q.s: The first Telugu inscription, the Kalamalla inscription (c. 575 CE), was issued by:
q.x: The Kalamalla (Kadapa) record of the Renati Chola Dhanunjaya Varma is the first Telugu inscription; Erragudipadu is the first fully available one.

q.s: The Kalamalla inscription, the first Telugu inscription, is found in which district?
q.x: Kalamalla is in Kadapa district; it dates to about 575 CE.

q.s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, commander of which Eastern Chalukya king?
q.x: Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription, an early Telugu verse record.

q.s: The Kakatiya capital Warangal was besieged in 1310 and Prataparudra made a tributary by:
q.x: Malik Kafur, Alauddin Khalji's general, besieged Warangal in 1310.

q.s: The Bayyaram tank inscription, which gives the best genealogy of the Kakatiyas, was issued by:
q.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister, traces the line from Venna.

q.s: Rani Rudrama Devi ruled the Kakatiya kingdom under the male name of:
q.x: She was co-regent from 1258 as Rudradeva Maharaja; she is ranked the second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, 'Golusukattu cheruvulu' referred to:
q.x: Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks; tank-building was one of the Sapta Santanalu.

q.s: Mahmud Gawan was the wazir of which Bahmani Sultan?
q.x: Mahmud Gawan served Muhammad Shah III; he divided the four tarafs into eight provinces.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Mahmud Gawan merged the eight tarafs into four provinces.
Mahmud Gawan was a leader of the Dakhni (local) faction.
Mahmud Gawan divided the four tarafs of the Bahmani kingdom into eight provinces.
Mahmud Gawan crushed the Telangana revolts with Reddi help.
q.x: Gawan, an Afaqi (Persian) noble, split the four tarafs into eight and used Velama help in Telangana.

q.s: Which of the following regional Sultanates was founded earliest?
q.x: Bengal (1342) came first, then Bahmani (1347), Malwa (1401) and Gujarat (1407).

q.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya II, was the envoy of:
q.x: Abdur Razzaq was the envoy of the Timurid Shah Rukh.

q.s: The literary hall of Krishnadevaraya was known as:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya's literary hall was Bhuvana Vijayam; Devaraya II's was the Mutyala Sala.

q.s: In Vijayanagara revenue records, 'Nanja' land meant:
q.x: Nanja was wet land, Punja dry land, Bagayati garden land and Banjara waste land.

q.s: The emblem of the Matsyas of Oddadi was:
q.x: The Matsyas of Oddadi, in the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram uplands, had the double-fish emblem.

q.s: The Gundeswara temple at Buddapuram was built by Kuppambika, wife of:
q.x: Kuppambika, wife of Malyala Gunda, built the Gundeswara temple at Buddapuram.

q.s: Which foreign traveller described the Mahanavami festival at Vijayanagara in detail?
q.x: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese visitor under Krishnadevaraya, described the Mahanavami and its sacrifices.

q.s: Which of the following foreigners did NOT visit the Vijayanagara empire?
q.x: Megasthenes came to the Mauryan court; Conti, Razzaq and Paes described Vijayanagara.

q.s: The largest gold coin of the Vijayanagara empire, also called Pagoda, was:
q.x: The Varaha (Pagoda, Gadyana, Honnu) was the largest gold coin; the small Panam was the most used.

q.s: The Battle of Chandurthi (1758), which brought the Northern Circars under English control, saw Forde defeat:
q.x: Colonel Forde defeated the French under Conflans at Chandurthi.

q.s: After the Battle of Tallikota (1565), the Vijayanagara capital was moved to:
q.x: After Tallikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) the capital shifted to Penugonda.

q.s: Who called Kandukuri Veeresalingam the 'Vidyasagar of South India'?
q.x: M.G. Ranade called Veeresalingam the 'Vidyasagar of South India'.

q.s: Colin Mackenzie, the collector of manuscripts and records of South India, became in 1815:
o: The first Surveyor General of India
q.x: Colin Mackenzie became the first Surveyor General of India in 1815.

q.s: In the usage of Europeans in the Madras Presidency, the word 'Gentoo' referred to:
q.x: 'Gentoo', probably from Portuguese 'gentio', meant Telugu; William Brown's Grammar of the Gentoo Language (1817) is a Telugu grammar.

q.s: The first district association in Andhra, formed in 1892, was that of:
q.x: The Krishna district association (1892) came first; Vizag followed in 1893 and Godavari in 1895.

q.s: The Godavari district association at Rajahmundry (1895) was founded by:
q.x: Nyapathi Subbarao founded the Godavari district association at Rajahmundry in 1895.

q.s: In the zamindari and agency areas of Andhra, 'Pullari' was a tax levied on:
q.x: Pullari was the grazing tax; vetti was forced free labour and nazarana the renewal fee for tenancy.

q.s: The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was founded in 1929 by:
q.x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded it and brought out the weekly Hunkar; the Oudh Kisan Sabha (1920) was Baba Ramchandra's.

q.s: The founding session of the All India Progressive Writers' Association at Lucknow in 1936 was presided over by:
q.x: Premchand presided over the first AIPWA session at Lucknow (1936).

q.s: Virasam (Viplava Rachayitala Sangham) was formed in 1970 at:
q.x: Virasam was formed at Hyderabad in July 1970; Arasam's first conference was at Tenali.

q.s: 'Anantham' is the autobiography of:
q.x: Anantham is Sri Sri's autobiography; Maro Prasthanam belongs to his revolutionary phase.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Sri Sri?
q.x: Gabbilam is by Gurram Jashuva.

q.s: The Telugu play 'Varavikrayam', written against the dowry system, was written by:
q.x: Kallakuri Narayana Rao wrote Varavikrayam; Prataparudriyam is by Vedam Venkataraya Sastri.

q.s: Andhra Patrika, founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, was first published in 1908 from:
q.x: Andhra Patrika began as a weekly from Bombay on 9 September 1908 and became a daily in 1914.

q.s: The Crescent, an English paper of Madras, was founded by:
q.x: Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded The Crescent in Madras.

q.s: Which tribal language of Andhra Pradesh has its own script?
q.x: Savara, a Munda language, is the only AP tribal language with its own script; Koya and Konda are Dravidian.

q.s: Which of the following languages does NOT belong to the Munda family?
q.x: Koya is a Dravidian language; Savara, Gadaba and Santali are Munda (Austro-Asiatic).

q.s: 'Gussadi' is a traditional dance of which tribe?
q.x: Gussadi is the Gond dance; Kommu is the Koya dance.

q.s: Among the Chenchus, the village office of 'Raju' is associated with which clan?
q.x: The Raju comes from the Bhoomani clan and the Mantri from the Kumakula clan.

q.s: The Bashir Bagh firing of 28 August 2000 in Hyderabad occurred during the agitation against:
q.x: Left parties and farmers were protesting against power tariff hikes under power-sector reforms.

q.s: Ramoji Film City, recognised by Guinness as the world's largest film studio complex, is located at:
q.x: Ramoji Film City, Hyderabad, is spread over about 1,666 acres.

q.s: The Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly was:
q.x: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser; Rajendra Prasad was President and Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: Rajendra Prasad was President of the Assembly; the others were Drafting Committee members.

q.s: The Indo-Roman trade grew strongly after the Romans took control of Egypt in:
q.x: Rome's conquest of Egypt in 30 BCE and the use of the monsoon route made the 1st c. BCE-2nd c. CE the peak of the trade.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court declare instant triple talaq unconstitutional?
q.x: Shayara Bano (2017) struck down instant triple talaq; Navtej Singh Johar (2018) read down Section 377.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Westernisation, as explained by M.N. Srinivas, is correct?
o: Srinivas regarded it as a morally good process.
It refers to changes brought about by over 150 years of British rule.
It is a universal process not tied to any particular source.
It covers only changes in technology.
q.x: Westernisation refers to changes under British rule; Srinivas saw it as ethically neutral and covering technology, institutions, ideology and values. It is source-specific, unlike modernisation.

q.s: Mizoram became a full-fledged State in 1987 following the Mizo Accord of:
q.x: The Mizo Accord was signed in 1986 and Mizoram became a State in 1987.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT become a full-fledged State in 1987?
q.x: Nagaland became a State on 1 December 1963; Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa became States in 1987.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for reservation of one-third of seats for women in Municipalities?
q.x: Article 243T covers Municipalities; Article 243D covers Panchayats.

q.s: The Telugu poem 'Gabbilam' (1941), a protest against untouchability, was written by:
q.x: Gurram Jashuva wrote Gabbilam: a bat can enter the temple, but an untouchable cannot.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Jyotiba Phule?
q.x: Annihilation of Caste (1936) is by B.R. Ambedkar; the other three are Phule's.

q.s: Seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha are filled through:
q.x: Reserved seats are filled by joint electorates of all voters; the 104th Amendment extended the reservation to 2030.

q.s: The 104th Constitutional Amendment (2019) ended the nomination of members of which community to the Lok Sabha?
q.x: The 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination and extended SC/ST reservation to 2030.

q.s: The Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad, begun in 1614, was completed in 1693 by:
q.x: It was begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah and completed by Aurangzeb after the fall of Golconda (1687).

q.s: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act came into force in:
q.x: The Act came into force on 23 December 1986, following the Gurupadaswamy Committee (1979) of the Ministry of Labour.

q.s: In Theodore Lowi's classification, a progressive income tax is an example of which type of policy?
q.x: Progressive tax and land reform are redistributive; licensing is regulatory and creating NITI Aayog is constitutive.

q.s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, the maximum monthly maintenance allowance is:
q.x: The cap is Rs 10,000 a month; the 2019 Amendment Bill to remove it lapsed.

q.s: Under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, bonded labourers are identified and freed mainly by:
q.x: District Vigilance Committees identify, free and rehabilitate bonded labourers; the Act of 1976 followed the 1975 Ordinance.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Gram Sabhas are the authority to identify and free bonded labourers.
The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was passed in 1976.
The 2016 rehabilitation scheme is funded equally by the Centre and the States.
The bonded labour Ordinance was issued in 1986.
q.x: The 1975 Ordinance became the 1976 Act; Vigilance Committees identify bonded labour and the 2016 scheme is fully Central.

q.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at:
q.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

q.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan brings about convergence of all the following EXCEPT:
q.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan converges ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat, not the Jal Jeevan Mission.

q.s: VB-G RAM G, the scheme introduced in December 2025, was meant to replace:
q.x: VB-G RAM G was introduced on 16 December 2025 to replace MGNREGA; it guarantees 125 days of work.

q.s: YSR Cheyutha (2020) gave Rs 18,750 a year to BC, SC, ST and minority women of which age group?
q.x: YSR Cheyutha covered women aged 45-60; YSR Kapu Nestham gave Rs 15,000 a year.

q.s: Under the AP Official Language Act, 1966, Urdu was made a second official language under which Section?
q.x: Section 7 made Urdu a second official language in specified districts; a 2022 amendment extended it to all districts.

q.s: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 was repealed in:
q.x: It was repealed in 1952, and the communities were 'denotified'; the Renke Commission (2008) was the first on DNTs.

q.s: The first national commission on Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes was headed by:
q.x: The Renke Commission (2008) was the first; the Idate Commission came later.

q.s: Which scheme provides free aids and assistive devices to persons with disabilities below an income ceiling?
q.x: ADIP provides aids and appliances; SIPDA funds implementation of the RPwD Act and DDRS funds NGOs.

q.s: MILAN 2026, the multilateral naval exercise, was held at:
q.x: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: India became the 27th signatory of the Artemis Accords in:
q.x: India signed the Artemis Accords in June 2023 as the 27th signatory.

q.s: The GE F414 jet engines for India are to be co-produced with:
q.x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited.

q.s: Which of the following UN bodies is NOT headquartered at Geneva?
q.x: UNICEF is headquartered in New York; UNESCO is in Paris.

q.s: The International Labour Organization is noted for its unique tripartite structure of:
q.x: ILO bodies bring together governments, employers and workers.

q.s: Who is the first woman and first African Director-General of the WTO?
q.x: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria began her second term on 1 September 2025.

q.s: Pascal Lamy, Director-General of the WTO during 2005-2013, is from:
q.x: Pascal Lamy is French, a former EU Trade Commissioner.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of India's relationship with international groupings?
o: India is a founding member of the Commonwealth's modern form
India is a member of BIMSTEC
India is a member of the OECD
India is a member of the SCO
q.x: India is not an OECD member, only a key partner; it belongs to the Commonwealth, BIMSTEC and the SCO.

q.s: The International Day of Yoga was first observed on 21 June of:
q.x: The UNGA resolution of 11 December 2014 set up the Day, first observed in 2015.

q.s: The idea of a 'Republic' in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
q.x: The ideals of Republic and liberty, equality, fraternity came from France.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was NOT borrowed from Britain?
q.x: Fundamental Rights were taken from the US Constitution; the others came from Britain.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT nominated by Lord Canning to the Legislative Council under the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
q.x: Canning nominated the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao.

q.s: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
q.x: J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee; Patel chaired the Advisory Committee.

q.s: Who was the first person to preside over the Constituent Assembly as its temporary President?
q.x: Sachchidananda Sinha presided first; Rajendra Prasad was the elected permanent President.

q.s: The first Official Language Commission (1955), set up under Article 344, was chaired by:
q.x: B.G. Kher chaired it; its report was reviewed by a parliamentary committee under G.B. Pant.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Official Language Commission was set up under Article 343.
The Kher Commission report was reviewed by a committee under Lal Bahadur Shastri.
The Official Languages Act, 1963 allowed English to continue alongside Hindi after 1965.
English ceased to be used for Union purposes from 1965.
q.x: The 1963 Act kept English after 1965; the Kher report was reviewed under G.B. Pant and the Commission came under Article 344.

q.s: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 143 lets the President seek the Supreme Court's opinion; Article 110 defines a Money Bill.

q.s: Which of the following Article–subject pairs is NOT correct?
o: Article 143 – Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
q.x: Article 340 deals with a Commission for Backward Classes; the Finance Commission is under Article 280.

q.s: The holy book of the Parsis is:
q.x: The Zend Avesta is the Parsi scripture; their highest grade of fire temple is the Atash Behram.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Parsis?
q.x: A Gurdwara is a Sikh place of worship; Atash Behram and Agiary are Parsi fire temples.

q.s: Which clause of Article 16 enables reservation in promotion for SCs and STs?
q.x: Article 16(4A) (77th Amendment, 1995) allows reservation in promotion; 16(4B) deals with carried-forward backlog vacancies.

q.s: The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 replaced the:
q.x: The LARR Act replaced the 1894 Act and made Social Impact Assessment compulsory.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Social Impact Assessment is compulsory under the LARR Act, 2013.
Compensation under the LARR Act can be up to two times market value in rural areas.
Acquired land left unused can never be returned to its owners.
The LARR Act amended but did not replace the 1894 Act.
q.x: SIA is compulsory; compensation is up to four times in rural areas and unused land is returned after five years.

q.s: The Supreme Court guidelines in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997) relate to:
q.x: D.K. Basu laid down safeguards on arrest and detention; Francis Coralie (1981) read dignity into Article 21.

q.s: The 10 per cent reservation for the economically weaker sections was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 103rd Amendment (2019) introduced EWS reservation, over and above the 50 per cent ceiling.

q.s: In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court upheld EWS reservation by a majority of:
q.x: A five-judge bench upheld it 3:2; CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissented.

q.s: Which was the first State to implement the 10 per cent EWS quota in 2019?
q.x: Gujarat implemented EWS reservation first, from 14 January 2019.

q.s: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 came into force on:
q.x: The RTE Act, giving effect to Article 21A, came into force on 1 April 2010.

q.s: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged which of the following schemes?
q.x: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education; RUSA is a higher-education scheme.

q.s: India's first National Policy on Education was adopted in:
q.x: The first NPE came in 1968, based on the Kothari Commission; the second in 1986.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment changed the word 'Oriya' to 'Odia'?
q.x: The 96th Amendment (2011) changed 'Oriya' to 'Odia'; the 93rd inserted Article 15(5).

q.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment–subject pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The NJAC came by the 99th Amendment (2014); the 101st introduced GST.

q.s: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament mainly examines:
o: The budget estimates before they are passed
The working of public sector undertakings
The audit reports of the CAG on government expenditure
q.x: The PAC examines CAG audit reports, a post-mortem check on expenditure; its recommendations are advisory.

q.s: Under Article 72, the form of clemency that removes both the sentence and the conviction is:
q.x: A pardon wipes out both sentence and conviction; commutation substitutes a lighter punishment.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment added the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry to the Presidential electoral college?
q.x: The 70th Amendment (1992) included the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies.

q.s: Who among the following does NOT take part in the election of the President of India?
o: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha
Elected members of the Rajya Sabha
Elected members of the Delhi Assembly
Elected members of the Lok Sabha
q.x: Nominated members of either House do not vote in the Presidential election.

q.s: The maximum period for which President's Rule under Article 356 can continue is:
q.x: It can last at most three years, in six-month extensions; beyond one year only with a National Emergency and an EC certificate.

q.s: Under which Article can the Governor reserve a Bill passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President?
q.x: Article 200 deals with assent to Bills, including reservation for the President; Article 201 covers the President's action.

q.s: Judges of a High Court, including acting judges, hold office until the age of:
q.x: High Court judges retire at 62; additional judges are appointed for up to two years.

q.s: Appeals against orders of the National Company Law Tribunal lie to the:
q.x: NCLT orders go to the NCLAT, which also hears appeals under the IBC and from the CCI.

q.s: CESTAT hears disputes relating to:
q.x: CESTAT deals with customs, excise and service tax; income tax disputes go to the ITAT.

q.s: The Cyber Appellate Tribunal was merged into TDSAT by the:
q.x: The Finance Act, 2017 merged the Cyber Appellate Tribunal into TDSAT.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Central Administrative Tribunal is correct?
o: It is guided by the principles of natural justice.
It is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
An applicant must be represented by a lawyer.
It hears disputes of private sector employees.
q.x: CAT is not bound by the CPC and follows natural justice; applicants may appear in person, and it deals with public servants.

q.s: The 1975 National Emergency, proclaimed on 25 June 1975, was withdrawn on:
q.x: The Emergency was withdrawn on 21 March 1977; 25 June is now observed as Samvidhan Hatya Diwas.

q.s: Under Article 246(4), for areas not included in any State, Parliament can make laws on matters in:
o: The Union and Concurrent Lists only
q.x: For Union Territories Parliament may legislate on any matter, including those in the State List.

q.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 is chaired by:
q.x: The Prime Minister chairs it; it decides by consensus and its recommendations are not binding.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: When the Chairman's post is vacant, the senior-most member automatically acts as Chairman.
The 41st Amendment raised the retirement age of UPSC members.
UPSC members retire at 65 and State PSC members at 62.
UPSC members can be removed by the Chief Justice of India.
q.x: UPSC members retire at 65, State PSC members at 62; an acting Chairman is appointed and only the President can remove members.

q.s: The Zonal Councils were set up under the:
q.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under Section 15 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

q.s: Which of the following bodies was set up by an executive order and NOT by a statute?
q.x: The National Security Council (1998) was created by an executive order; the others rest on statutes.

q.s: 'Mahila Jan Sunwai', a public hearing of women's grievances, is organised by the:
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: The NCW organises Mahila Jan Sunwai; it is a recommendatory body with no power to punish.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The NCW can impose criminal sentences on violators of women's rights.
The National Commission for Women is a recommendatory body and cannot punish offenders.
The NCW was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
The NCW was created by a Constitutional Amendment.
q.x: The NCW is a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990, with recommendatory powers only.

q.s: After the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson of the NHRC holds office for a term of:
o: Five years or up to 70 years of age
Five years or up to 65 years of age
Three years or up to 70 years of age
Three years or up to 65 years of age
q.x: The 2019 amendment set the term at three years or 70 years of age.

q.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status under Article:
q.x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B for the NCBC; Article 338A is the NCST.

q.s: Following the 2019 amendment of the Protection of Human Rights Act, a State Human Rights Commission can be chaired by:
o: Only a retired Chief Justice of a High Court
Only a retired Supreme Court Judge
A retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court
q.x: Since 2019 a High Court Judge, besides a retired HC Chief Justice, can chair an SHRC.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court lay down the categories of 'rarest of rare' cases weighing aggravating and mitigating factors?
q.x: Machhi Singh (1983) set out the categories; Shatrughan Chauhan (2014) held that inordinate delay in mercy justifies commutation.

q.s: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000) was chaired by:
q.x: Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah chaired the NCRWC, which reported in 2002.

q.s: Under the FRBM Act (as amended in 2018), the Central Government's debt target is:
q.x: The target is 40% of GDP for the Centre and 60% for general government; the fiscal deficit cap is 3%.

q.s: A major criticism of replacing enforceable welfare rights with discretionary cash transfers is that it:
q.x: Discretionary transfers cannot be claimed as of right, so beneficiaries lose bargaining power and become passive recipients.

q.s: The DMK was formed in 1949 by C.N. Annadurai after breaking away from:
q.x: The DMK emerged in 1949 from Periyar's Dravidar Kazhagam.

q.s: The Republican Party of India, inspired by Ambedkar's ideas, was formed in:
q.x: The RPI was formed in 1957, after Ambedkar's death in 1956.

q.s: The Communist Party of India formally took shape at a conference held in December 1925 at:
q.x: The CPI was formally founded at the Kanpur Conference on 26 December 1925; it completed 100 years in 2025.

q.s: Under MPLADS, the works recommended by a Member of Parliament are executed by the:
q.x: The District Authority executes MPLADS works; they are monitored on the eSAKSHI portal.

q.s: Village and ward secretariats with volunteers were introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
q.x: The village/ward secretariat and volunteer system started in 2019.

q.s: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme was launched in:
q.x: ICDS began in 1975; the National Extension Service in 1953 and Food for Work in 1977.

q.s: Lord Ripon's resolution on local self-government was issued in:
q.x: Ripon's resolution of 18 May 1882 made him the 'father of local self-government'; Mayo's 1870 resolution was on financial decentralisation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an item in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: Public order is a State List subject, not a Panchayat item; urban planning is in the Twelfth Schedule.

q.s: The intermediate tier of Panchayati Raj in Andhra Pradesh is known as:
q.x: AP has the Mandal (Praja) Parishad; Janpad is MP's, Kshetra UP's and Taluka Gujarat's.

q.s: Which of the following intermediate-tier names is NOT correctly matched with its State?
q.x: Kerala has Block Panchayats; Taluka Panchayat is the Gujarat name.

q.s: A Tribes Advisory Council under the Fifth Schedule consists of not more than:
q.x: It has up to 20 members, three-fourths of whom are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Three-fourths of a Tribes Advisory Council are ST members of the Lok Sabha.
A Tribes Advisory Council can be set up only in States having Scheduled Areas.
The Fifth Schedule applies to the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Parliament can amend the Fifth Schedule by ordinary law.
q.x: The Fifth Schedule is amendable by ordinary law; TAC members are ST MLAs; those four States are under the Sixth Schedule.

q.s: Which committee described Panchayati Raj institutions as 'grass without roots'?
q.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) used the phrase; Ashok Mehta recommended a two-tier system.

q.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) recommended a Panchayati Raj structure of:
o: Two tiers – Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat
q.x: Ashok Mehta suggested a two-tier system of Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat.

q.s: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation is divided into zones headed by:
q.x: GVMC has zonal commissioners for its zones.

q.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in which goal?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in SDG 7; it scored 74 as a 'Front Runner'.

q.s: The rupee became fully convertible on the current account in August 1994 when India accepted Article VIII of the Articles of Agreement of the:
q.x: India accepted Article VIII of the IMF in 1994; the rupee is still not fully convertible on the capital account.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The rupee became fully convertible on the capital account in 2006.
The rupee is fully convertible on the current account but not on the capital account.
Under the LRS individuals may remit up to $25,000 a year.
Current account convertibility was adopted in July 1991.
q.x: India adopted current account convertibility in 1994; capital account convertibility is still partial and the LRS limit is $250,000.

q.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India functions under the:
q.x: IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016 under the IBC and functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

q.s: Which body insures bank deposits in India?
q.x: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation insures bank deposits; NFRA oversees auditing standards.

q.s: The committee on revisiting and revitalising the PPP model of infrastructure (2015) was headed by:
q.x: The Vijay Kelkar Committee proposed an IPRC and an IPAT, and discouraged the Swiss-challenge method.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: It recommended an Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal.
It encouraged PSUs to bid for PPP projects.
It recommended that PPP contracts should never be renegotiated.
q.x: Kelkar proposed IPRC and IPAT, a renegotiation mechanism, and discouraged Swiss challenge and PSU bidding.

q.s: The Bhogapuram international airport in Andhra Pradesh is located in which district?
q.x: Bhogapuram (Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport) is in Vizianagaram district, built by GMR on PPP.

q.s: The Machilipatnam port is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Machilipatnam port is in Krishna district; Mulapeta is in Srikakulam.

q.s: The 20th National Conference on e-Governance (2017) was held at:
q.x: Visakhapatnam hosted the 20th NCeG in January 2017; Shillong hosted the 22nd (2019).

q.s: City Gas Distribution networks in India are regulated by:
q.x: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board regulates CGD; AERA regulates aeronautical charges.

q.s: The UNDP index that compares female HDI with male HDI is the:
q.x: The GDI is the ratio of female to male HDI; the GII covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market.

q.s: According to Census 2011, India's literacy rate was:
q.x: Final Census 2011 literacy was 72.98% (74.04% was the provisional figure).

q.s: According to Census 2011, the gap between male and female literacy was the largest in:
q.x: Rajasthan had the widest gap; Meghalaya the smallest.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the most urbanised district of (residuary) Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Visakhapatnam was the most urbanised district and the largest urban agglomeration; AP's urban share (29.5%) was below the national 31.2%.

q.s: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was launched on 2 February 2006 in how many districts?
q.x: It began in 200 districts, added 130 in 2007-08 and covered all districts from 1 April 2008.

q.s: APTIDCO took a loan to complete 2.61 lakh houses in Andhra Pradesh from:
q.x: APTIDCO's loan for the 2.61 lakh houses came from HUDCO.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Dudekula community is included in the list of:
q.x: The Dudekula, a Muslim community, are in AP's BC list.

q.s: Jagananna Vasathi Deevena in Andhra Pradesh is meant to meet students':
q.x: Vasathi Deevena covers hostel costs while Vidya Deevena reimburses fees.

q.s: In Q1 of 2026-27, India's gross fixed capital formation as a share of GDP rose to:
q.x: GFCF rose to 34.3% of GDP from 31.4%; real GFCF grew 11.9%, faster than private consumption (7.1%).

q.s: The Human Development Index was introduced by the UNDP in:
q.x: UNDP introduced the HDI in 1990 (Mahbub ul Haq); it uses life expectancy at birth, education and GNI per capita at PPP.

q.s: The first State in India to publish a Human Development Report was:
q.x: Madhya Pradesh published the first State HDR in 1995.

q.s: The first Andhra Pradesh Human Development Report (2007) was prepared by:
q.x: The Centre for Economic and Social Studies (CESS), Hyderabad prepared it.

q.s: In India, Environmental Impact Assessment was first used in 1978 for:
q.x: EIA began in 1978 with river valley projects; the EIA Notification 2006 made clearance compulsory for listed categories.

q.s: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under the:
q.x: The Green Credit Rules were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

q.s: Which was the first Indian State to adopt a green GDP measure called Gross Environment Product (GEP)?
q.x: Uttarakhand adopted GEP; EnviStats India is brought out by MoSPI.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: EnviStats India is released by the RBI.
The SEEA Central Framework was adopted by the World Bank.
EnviStats India is brought out by MoSPI.
Kerala was the first State to adopt Gross Environment Product.
q.x: MoSPI publishes EnviStats; SEEA was adopted by the UN Statistical Commission and Uttarakhand adopted GEP first.

q.s: People who move in and out of poverty, such as seasonal workers, are described as being in:
q.x: Transient poverty refers to the churning poor; chronic poverty persists over long periods or generations.

q.s: The expert group that recommended State-specific poverty lines (1993) was headed by:
q.x: The Lakdawala Expert Group recommended State-specific lines; Dandekar and Rath wrote 'Poverty in India' (1971).

q.s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article:
q.x: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every five years with a Chairman and four members; its advice is not binding.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Finance Commission is constituted by Parliament every five years.
The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and six members.
The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 270.
The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory and not binding.
q.x: The President constitutes it under Article 280 with a Chairman and four members; its advice is not binding.

q.s: 'Contribution to GDP', with a weight of 10%, was newly introduced as a devolution criterion by which Finance Commission?
q.x: The 16th FC introduced contribution to GDP (10%) and dropped tax and fiscal effort used by the 15th.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes to:
q.x: The 14th FC raised it to 42% and made no distinction between general and Special Category States.

q.s: In 2025 the RBI cut the Cash Reserve Ratio by 100 basis points to:
q.x: The CRR was cut to 3.0% of NDTL, releasing about Rs 2.5 lakh crore of liquidity.

q.s: Under the RBI's liquidity adjustment facility, the floor of the policy corridor is the:
q.x: The SDF rate is the floor and the MSF rate the ceiling of the LAF corridor.

q.s: In 2004, the limit for foreign direct investment in private sector banks in India was raised to:
q.x: FDI up to 74% was allowed in private banks in 2004.

q.s: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the largest item of 'rupee comes from' is:
q.x: Borrowings and other liabilities (24 paise) lead; income tax (21 paise) is the largest tax.

q.s: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts, used for trade settlement in rupees, are:
o: Dollar accounts of Indian banks abroad
Rupee accounts of foreign banks with Indian banks
Accounts of NRIs with the RBI
Accounts of exporters with EXIM Bank
q.x: SRVAs are rupee accounts of foreign banks with Indian banks, under the RBI framework of July 2022.

q.s: Operation Flood, which aimed at building a national milk grid, was launched by the NDDB in:
q.x: Operation Flood began in 1970 on the Anand model; the NDDB was set up by the Government of India in 1965.

q.s: The Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF) markets milk under the brand:
q.x: GCMMF markets under AMUL; Mother Dairy is an NDDB brand.

q.s: According to the Agriculture Census 2015-16, small and marginal holdings formed about what share of all holdings?
q.x: Small and marginal holdings were 86.2% of holdings but had only 47.3% of the operated area.

q.s: A Maharatna CPSE can invest without Government approval up to:
q.x: Maharatnas can invest up to Rs 5,000 crore per project; Navratnas up to Rs 1,000 crore or 15% of net worth.

q.s: Which scheme is credited with making almost all mobile phones used in India domestically manufactured?
q.x: Under Make in India and the PLI scheme about 99.2% of phones used in India are made in India.

q.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, penalties are imposed by the:
q.x: The Data Protection Board of India imposes penalties up to Rs 250 crore; the DPDP Rules were notified in November 2025.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act received assent in August 2023.
Penalties under the DPDP Act are imposed by MeitY.
The DPDP Rules have not yet been notified.
The maximum penalty under the DPDP Act is Rs 25 crore.
q.x: The Act received assent on 11 August 2023; the Board imposes penalties up to Rs 250 crore and the Rules came in November 2025.

q.s: Which is the largest State economy of India by GSDP?
q.x: Maharashtra is the largest State economy; AP ranks about 8th.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh joined the UDAY scheme for power distribution companies in:
q.x: AP signed UDAY on 24 June 2016 and took over about Rs 11,000 crore of DISCOM debt.

q.s: Revenue from the auction of mineral blocks under the MMDR Act accrues to:
q.x: States own minerals in their territory, conduct the auctions and receive the auction premium.

q.s: The proposed DESH legislation, meant to replace the SEZ Act, stands for:
o: Development of Export and Special Hubs
Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs
q.x: DESH (Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs) was announced in Budget 2022-23.

q.s: The IFFCO Kisan SEZ in Andhra Pradesh is located in which district?
q.x: IFFCO Kisan SEZ is at Nellore; Divi's is at Visakhapatnam and Parry at Kakinada.

q.s: Treasury Bills issued by the Government of India are:
o: Long-term securities of 10 years or more
Bonds paying a fixed half-yearly coupon
Zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount
Instruments issued only by State Governments
q.x: T-Bills are short-term, zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value.

q.s: Which of the following years was NOT a leap year?
q.x: A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400; 1900 is not, so it was not a leap year.

q.s: The standard meridian of Indian Standard Time (82°30'E) passes through:
q.x: IST is reckoned from Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, and is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a sedimentary rock?
q.x: Granite is an igneous rock; rock salt is chemically formed and shale and conglomerate are clastic sedimentary rocks.

q.s: In karst regions, a calcium-carbonate deposit hanging from the roof of a cave is called:
q.x: Stalactites hang from the roof; stalagmites rise from the floor; joined, they form a pillar.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a karst landform?
q.x: A drumlin is a glacial depositional landform; the others form in limestone (karst) regions.

q.s: The westerlies blowing between 40° and 50° South latitudes are known as the:
q.x: Roaring Forties blow at 40-50°S; the Furious Fifties at 50-60°S.

q.s: Most severe cyclones such as Hudhud and Titli have struck the Andhra Pradesh coast during:
q.x: Cyclones hit AP mostly in the post-monsoon season, October-December.

q.s: Cyclone Montha (October 2025) made landfall near:
q.x: Montha made landfall near Kakinada.

q.s: Ships in the deep sea are not much affected by a tsunami because in deep water a tsunami:
o: Has a very low wave height
q.x: In deep water a tsunami is a gentle rise and fall despite moving very fast; it grows in height near the shore.

q.s: Surface salinity of the oceans is the highest near:
q.x: Clear skies, high evaporation and low rain in the subtropical highs make salinity highest there.

q.s: The seven mandals transferred to Andhra Pradesh in 2014 to facilitate the Polavaram project were originally part of which district?
q.x: The seven mandals came from Khammam; Bhadrachalam town remained in Telangana.

q.s: The foundation stone of the capital city Amaravati was laid on:
q.x: The Amaravati foundation was laid on 22 October 2015.

q.s: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
q.x: The Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'; the Damodar was the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.

q.s: The Gandikota reservoir in Kadapa district is built on the river:
q.x: Gandikota reservoir is on the Penna.

q.s: The Telugu Ganga project, to supply drinking water to Chennai, was conceived under:
q.x: The Telugu Ganga project was conceived by N.T. Rama Rao.

q.s: The Pothireddypadu head regulator is located at the start of the:
q.x: Pothireddypadu is at the head of the Srisailam Right Main Canal.

q.s: The Godavari river rises at:
q.x: The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik; the Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a distributary of the Godavari delta?
q.x: Hamsaladeevi is where the Krishna meets the sea; Gautami, Vasishta and Vainateya are Godavari branches.

q.s: The dark colour of black (regur) soils is mainly due to:
q.x: The colour comes from titaniferous magnetite / iron and titanium compounds; black soils are neutral to alkaline.

q.s: The most fertile soils of Andhra Pradesh, renewed by river silt each year, are the:
o: Laterite soils of the Eastern Ghats
Deltaic alluvial soils of the Krishna-Godavari
q.x: Delta alluvium is renewed by fresh silt deposited by the rivers.

q.s: Topsoil loss due to podu (shifting) cultivation is a problem mainly in which districts of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam
q.x: Podu cultivation in the tribal hill districts of ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam strips topsoil.

q.s: The National Disaster Response Fund is provided for under which Section of the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
q.x: Section 46 covers the NDRF (fund); Section 47 the National Disaster Mitigation Fund and Section 48 State funds.

q.s: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the National Plan is prepared by the:
q.x: The National Executive Committee prepares the National Plan, approved by the NDMA.

q.s: The Interlinking of Rivers programme in India is implemented by the:
q.x: NWDA handles river interlinking; CWC handles surface water and floods and CGWB groundwater.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a part of the 'Lithium Triangle'?
q.x: The Lithium Triangle is Bolivia, Argentina and Chile; Australia is the largest producer of lithium.

q.s: Which country produces more than half of the world's nickel?
q.x: Indonesia produces over half of world nickel output.

q.s: The white marble used in the Taj Mahal and the Victoria Memorial came from:
q.x: Makrana in Rajasthan is famous for its fine white marble.

q.s: Phase-I of the Green Energy Corridor in Andhra Pradesh was funded by:
q.x: Phase-I of the Green Energy Corridor was funded by Germany's KfW.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a site of India's strategic petroleum reserves under ISPRL (Phase I)?
q.x: Phase-I reserves are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur (5.33 MMT); Phase-II is at Chandikhol and Padur.

q.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 in Paris (2015) by India and:
q.x: India and France launched the ISA; it is headquartered at Gurugram.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) targets annual green hydrogen production by 2030 of:
q.x: The target is 5 MMT of green hydrogen a year by 2030.

q.s: The 'Yellow Revolution' in India is associated with the production of:
q.x: The Yellow Revolution relates to oilseeds; horticulture and honey belong to the Golden Revolution.

q.s: The Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram industrial region is mainly known for:
q.x: Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram is known for cashew, coir and rubber; steel and shipbuilding belong to Visakhapatnam-Guntur.

q.s: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises was formed in 2007 by merging the Ministry of Small Scale Industries with the Ministry of:
q.x: The MSME Ministry was formed in 2007 by merging Small Scale Industries and Agro and Rural Industries.

q.s: Rayon, also called artificial silk, is made from:
q.x: Rayon is a cellulose fibre from wood pulp; pulp and paper is the largest forest-based industry.

q.s: The node of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC) in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Krishnapatnam in Nellore district is the CBIC node; Orvakal is on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the NICDIT-funded industrial nodes in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The NICDIT nodes are Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal; Bhogapuram is the new airport site.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is being developed with funding support from:
q.x: VCIC, India's first coastal corridor, is supported by the Asian Development Bank.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the four greenfield ports being developed in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The greenfield ports are Ramayapatnam, Machilipatnam, Mulapeta and Kakinada Gateway; Visakhapatnam is an existing major port.

q.s: The National Logistics Policy, launched in 2022, aims to place India in the Logistics Performance Index by 2030 among the top:
q.x: It aims for the top 25 by 2030; India ranked 38th in LPI 2023.

q.s: The Trans-Siberian Railway connects Moscow with:
q.x: The 9,289 km line runs from Moscow to Vladivostok, crossing 8 time zones.

q.s: India Post Payments Bank was launched on 1 September 2018 under the:
q.x: IPPB functions under the Department of Posts.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Project Arrow (2008) aimed at upgrading post offices.
India Post Payments Bank was launched in 2015.
IPPB functions under the Department of Financial Services.
q.x: Project Arrow upgraded post offices; Speed Post began in 1986 and IPPB (2018) is under the Department of Posts.

q.s: The National Fossil Wood Park at Tiruvakkarai is located in:
q.x: Tiruvakkarai is in Tamil Nadu; the Nomira pillow lava site is in Odisha.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven anchor hubs of the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy 2024-29?
q.x: The anchor hubs are Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Araku, Rajahmundry, Amaravati, Srisailam and Gandikota.

q.s: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), developed by Morris D. Morris, is based on literacy, life expectancy and:
q.x: PQLI combines literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy at age one.

q.s: Which of the following indices is NOT published by the UNDP?
q.x: PQLI was developed by Morris D. Morris; the HDI, GII and GDI are UNDP indices.

q.s: The Economic Survey of which year warned of a 'demographic nightmare' if the demographic dividend is not backed by health, skills and jobs?
q.x: The Economic Survey 2018-19 used the phrase.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the sex ratio of residual (13-district) Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Residual AP had 997; undivided AP had 993. The ST sex ratio in AP is 1,009.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the number of people living in slums in India was about:
q.x: Census 2011 counted about 6.54 crore slum dwellers.

q.s: The HRIDAY scheme covered how many heritage cities, including Amaravati?
q.x: HRIDAY covered 12 heritage cities; the Smart Cities Mission covers 100 cities.

q.s: The EAC-PM estimate that about 63% of India was urban (2015) was based on:
q.x: The EAC-PM used satellite (built-up area) data; the World Bank (2010) put 'urban-like' areas at 55.3%.

q.s: Which scholar classified the Indian population on the basis of waves of migration (1931)?
q.x: J.H. Hutton, Census Commissioner of 1931, based his scheme on waves of migration; Haddon used hair form.

q.s: According to Census 2011, Telugu ranks in terms of number of speakers in India:
q.x: Telugu fell to fourth, behind Hindi, Bengali and Marathi.

q.s: According to Malthus, population increases in:
q.x: Malthus (1798) held that population grows geometrically and food supply arithmetically.

q.s: According to Malthus, which of the following is NOT a positive check on population?
q.x: Late marriage and moral restraint are preventive checks; positive checks raise the death rate.

q.s: The first 'Vigyan Ratna' under the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (2024) was awarded to:
q.x: Biochemist G. Padmanabhan received the first Vigyan Ratna.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Bhatnagar Prize continues as the Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar award.
The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar covers 10 domains.
The Vigyan Team award is given to a single researcher.
The Bhatnagar Prize has been abolished altogether.
q.x: The Bhatnagar Prize lives on as Vigyan Yuva-SSB; the RVP covers 13 domains and Vigyan Team goes to teams of three or more.

q.s: The Science and Technology Policy 2003 aimed to raise India's gross expenditure on R&D to:
q.x: The 2003 policy targeted GERD of 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan.

q.s: In blockchain technology, each block contains transactions, a timestamp and:
o: The name of the central validator
The hash of the previous block
The IP address of the miner
q.x: A block links to the earlier one through its hash, making the chain immutable.

q.s: The fern Pteris vittata is used in phytoremediation to remove:
q.x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Alyssum accumulates nickel and sunflower uranium.

q.s: LTE and VoLTE technologies belong to which generation of mobile telecommunication?
q.x: LTE and VoLTE are 4G technologies; 5G New Radio offers latency as low as 1 ms.

q.s: The LVM3-M2 mission of October 2022 placed 36 satellites of which company into orbit?
q.x: LVM3-M2 was LVM3's first commercial launch, carrying 36 OneWeb satellites (about 5,796 kg) to low Earth orbit.

q.s: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission uses which radar frequency bands?
q.x: NISAR uses L-band (NASA) and S-band (ISRO) and can detect centimetre-scale ground movement.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: InSAR compares the amplitude of optical images.
InSAR detects ground deformation by comparing the phase of radar images.
NISAR uses the C-band and X-band.
NISAR can detect only metre-scale movements.
q.x: InSAR uses phase differences; NISAR uses L- and S-bands and detects centimetre-scale motion.

q.s: An astronaut in an orbiting spacecraft feels weightless because:
o: The craft and astronaut fall freely with the same acceleration
The spacecraft moves at constant velocity
q.x: Both are in free fall together, so the normal force (felt weight) is zero; gravity still acts.

q.s: The 'Zircon' hypersonic missile belongs to which country?
q.x: Zircon is a Russian ship-launched hypersonic missile; Spyder is Israeli and Minuteman III American.

q.s: Which of the following missiles is NOT indigenously developed by India?
q.x: Spyder is an Israeli (Rafael) air-defence system used by the IAF.

q.s: BrahMos, the India-Russia cruise missile, is a:
q.x: BrahMos is supersonic (Mach 2.8-3.0) with a solid booster and liquid ramjet; its range grew after India joined the MTCR in 2016.

q.s: Hindustan Shipyard at Visakhapatnam was set up in 1941 by:
q.x: Scindia Steam Navigation Company founded it in 1941.

q.s: India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell ferry was built by:
q.x: Cochin Shipyard built it; it was flagged off virtually from Thoothukudi.

q.s: The first Aadhaar village of India, where numbers were issued on 29 September 2010, is:
q.x: Tembhli in Nandurbar, Maharashtra was the first Aadhaar village.

q.s: Publicly sharing a person's private information online without consent is called:
q.x: Doxxing exposes private details; trolling is deliberately provocative content.

q.s: 'Mana Mitra' of the Andhra Pradesh Government is a platform for:
q.x: Mana Mitra delivers government services over WhatsApp; Disha SOS is the women's safety app.

q.s: In a digital signature system, the sender signs a document using:
q.x: The sender signs with his private key and the receiver verifies with the public key.

q.s: Asia's first research reactor, which attained criticality in 1956 at Trombay, was:
q.x: Apsara (1956) came first, followed by CIRUS (1960), Dhruva (1985) and KAMINI (1996).

q.s: Which of the following functions directly under the Prime Minister?
q.x: The Department of Atomic Energy is directly under the PM; MNRE took its present name in 2006.

q.s: The UDAY scheme (2015) for financial turnaround of power distribution companies was launched by the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
q.x: UDAY was launched by the Ministry of Power and aimed to cut AT&C losses to 15%.

q.s: India leapfrogged from BS-IV directly to BS-VI emission norms nationwide with effect from:
q.x: BS-VI came into force nationwide on 1 April 2020, skipping BS-V; BS-II first applied in Delhi from 1 April 2000.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: BS-III norms were applied nationwide on 1 April 2005.
India applied BS-V norms nationwide in 2018.
BS-IV norms were introduced in 2010 in 23 cities.
BS-II norms were first applied in Delhi from 1 April 2000.
q.x: BS-II began in Delhi in 2000; BS-III in 2005 only in 11 cities, BS-IV in 2010 in 13 cities, and BS-V was skipped.

q.s: The installed capacity of the Polavaram hydroelectric project is:
q.x: Polavaram hydel project is 960 MW; Upper Sileru is 240 MW.

q.s: The CEA plan up to 2035-36 envisages a total energy storage capacity of about:
q.x: It envisages 174 GW: 94 GW pumped storage and 80 GW BESS.

q.s: The PM-KUSUM scheme mainly provides for:
o: Solar pumps and solar power for farmers
q.x: PM-KUSUM supports solar pumps for farmers; AP's target is 2.93 lakh pumps.

q.s: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is located at:
q.x: Kurnool UMSP (1,000 MW) is at Gani-Sakunala, Panyam mandal; NP Kunta is Ananthapuram-I.

q.s: The koala, which feeds almost only on eucalyptus leaves, is an example of a:
o: Specialist species with a narrow niche
q.x: A specialist has a narrow niche breadth; the niche is a species' functional role, its habitat the address.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Competing species can coexist by partitioning a shared resource.
The niche of a species is its physical address.
The realised niche is the full range of conditions a species could use without competitors.
Generalist species have a narrow niche breadth.
q.x: Resource partitioning allows coexistence; the niche is a functional role and the full potential range is the fundamental niche.

q.s: In a food chain, herbivores occupy which trophic level?
q.x: Producers are first, herbivores (primary consumers) second and secondary consumers third.

q.s: In terrestrial ecosystems, the major part of energy flows through the:
q.x: On land more energy flows through the detritus chain; in water the grazing chain dominates.

q.s: Which State of India has the second-largest mangrove ecosystem (Godavari and Krishna estuaries)?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks second; West Bengal (Sundarbans) has the largest mangrove cover.

q.s: Which of the following is a sedimentary biogeochemical cycle?
q.x: The phosphorus cycle has no atmospheric phase; its reservoir is phosphate rock in the Earth's crust.

q.s: India's Citrus Gene Sanctuary is located in the:
q.x: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary is in Nokrek, Garo Hills, Meghalaya.

q.s: N.I. Vavilov identified how many centres of origin of cultivated plants?
q.x: Vavilov identified eight centres; rice, sugarcane and mango belong to the Hindustan centre.

q.s: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: They were inscribed in 2012 as a serial site of 39 component areas in seven clusters.

q.s: The UN-REDD Programme (2008) is run jointly by FAO, UNDP and:
q.x: UN-REDD is run by FAO, UNDP and UNEP.

q.s: India's first community REDD+ project, the Khasi Hills project, is located in:
q.x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ Project is in Meghalaya, Plan Vivo certified.

q.s: The '30x30' target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework aims to:
o: Conserve 30% of land and oceans by 2030
q.x: 30x30 (Target 3) is to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030.

q.s: Under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, Target 16 seeks to:
q.x: Target 16 is on sustainable consumption, including halving food waste; Target 6 deals with invasive species.

q.s: The International Big Cat Alliance, launched by India, covers how many big cat species?
q.x: IBCA covers seven big cats, including jaguar and puma; its secretariat is in India.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
q.x: IBCA covers tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.

q.s: Under solid waste segregation rules, paper, plastics, metals and glass go into the:
q.x: These recyclables are dry waste; special care is for domestic hazardous waste.

q.s: Itai-itai disease, first reported in Toyama, Japan, is caused by poisoning from:
q.x: Itai-itai is cadmium poisoning; Minamata disease is methyl mercury poisoning.

q.s: 'Blue baby syndrome' (methaemoglobinaemia) is caused by excess of which substance in drinking water?
q.x: Nitrate causes blue baby syndrome; excess fluoride causes knock-knee (skeletal fluorosis).

q.s: Kolleru Lake, under stress from eutrophication, lies between the deltas of:
q.x: Kolleru lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas; aquaculture ponds and farm runoff pollute it.

q.s: In Vanashakti (May 2025), the Supreme Court held that retrospective (ex post facto) environmental clearance is:
q.x: Vanashakti called retrospective EC a 'gross illegality'.

q.s: Assessment of the environmental effects of policies, plans and programmes is called:
q.x: SEA addresses policies, plans and programmes; LCA studies a product from cradle to grave.

q.s: Under the Stockholm Convention on POPs, DDT is listed in Annex B because:
o: Its limited use for malaria control is allowed
q.x: Annex B restricts DDT but allows use for disease-vector control; dioxins and furans are in Annex C.

q.s: AquAdvantage, the first genetically modified animal approved for food, is a:
q.x: AquAdvantage is a GM Atlantic salmon that grows faster.

q.s: According to the WMO, the largest share of the rise in warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases during 1990-2024 came from:
q.x: CO2 drove about 81% of the rise; methane contributes about 16% of radiative forcing.

q.s: The Greenhouse Gas Bulletin is published annually by the:
q.x: The World Meteorological Organization publishes it; CO2 stood at 423.9 ppm in 2024.

q.s: The Clean Development Mechanism is provided for under which Article of the Kyoto Protocol?
q.x: CDM is under Article 12; Article 6 provides Joint Implementation and Article 17 emissions trading.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: CDM projects are run only in Annex I countries.
Certified Emission Reductions are issued by the CDM Executive Board.
The CDM is provided under Article 6 of the Kyoto Protocol.
The CDM was created under the Paris Agreement.
q.x: CERs come from the CDM Executive Board; CDM (Article 12, Kyoto) projects are in developing countries.

q.s: Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of NCDs (NP-NCD), population-based screening covers all persons above the age of:
q.x: Everyone above 30 is screened; NPCDCS was launched in 2010.

q.s: The first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to be certified malaria-free was:
q.x: The Maldives was first; Sri Lanka followed in 2016.

q.s: Under the National Health Mission, Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) provides:
q.x: JSY gives cash for institutional delivery; JSSK gives free (zero-expense) delivery and newborn care.

q.s: The CSIR laboratory that maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time is:
q.x: The National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi keeps IST; NEERI is at Nagpur and CSMCRI at Bhavnagar.

q.s: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) is located at:
q.x: NEERI, a CSIR lab, is at Nagpur.

q.s: Vigyan Prasar, the science communication body, is an autonomous organisation under the:
q.x: Vigyan Prasar (1989) is under DST; it runs the India Science channel.

q.s: Tele-MANAS, launched by the Government of India, provides:
q.x: Tele-MANAS is the national tele-mental health helpline; SWAYAM offers free online courses.

q.s: The largest segment of India's bioeconomy is the:
q.x: The industrial segment (47%) is larger than pharma (35%); the bioeconomy reached $165.7 billion in 2024.

q.s: According to the CEA, India's plan to add new coal-based capacity by 2035 is mainly meant to:
q.x: About 97 GW of new coal capacity is planned to balance variable renewable power and keep the grid stable.

q.s: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is at:
q.x: ADB is in Manila; the ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta.

q.s: The secretariat of the South Asia Wildlife Enforcement Network (SAWEN) is at:
q.x: SAWEN is based in Kathmandu; the CITES secretariat is in Geneva.

q.s: The 2025 SCO summit, which adopted the Tianjin Declaration, was held in:
q.x: The SCO summit was held at Tianjin, China, on 31 August-1 September 2025; it condemned the Pahalgam attack.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
q.x: Turkey is a dialogue partner; India and Pakistan joined in 2017 and Iran in 2023.

q.s: The Panchsheel principles were first formally signed in 1954 in an agreement between India and China relating to:
q.x: Panchsheel was signed on 29 April 1954 in the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with the Tibet Region; it entered the Bandung Ten Principles in 1955.

q.s: How many members does the East Asia Summit have?
q.x: The EAS has 18 members: 10 ASEAN states and 8 partners; the 20th EAS (2025) was held at Kuala Lumpur.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the East Asia Summit?
q.x: The EAS has 10 ASEAN members and 8 partners including India, USA and Russia; Pakistan is not a member.

q.s: IBSAMAR is a joint naval exercise of:
q.x: IBSA is India, Brazil and South Africa; the IBSA Fund is managed by UNOSSC.

q.s: COP31 of the UNFCCC, under a split presidency arrangement with Australia, is hosted by:
q.x: Türkiye hosts and presides over COP31 while Australia leads the negotiations.

q.s: The World Bank Group's 'Water Forward' initiative (April 2026) was launched by WBG President:
q.x: Ajay Banga launched Water Forward; the WBG is to reach 400 million of the targeted 1 billion people.

q.s: Ouagadougou is the capital of:
q.x: Ouagadougou is the capital of Burkina Faso; Victoria is the capital of Seychelles.

q.s: Which of the following country–capital pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The capital of Trinidad and Tobago is Port of Spain.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five institutions of the World Bank Group?
q.x: The WBG comprises IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID; the AIIB is a separate China-led bank.

q.s: The 14th Ministerial Conference of the WTO (March 2026) was held at:
q.x: MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, on 26-29 March 2026.

q.s: The term 'ecocide' was coined in 1970 by:
q.x: Biologist Arthur W. Galston coined the term in 1970.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Ecocide is listed as a separate core crime under Article 8 of the Rome Statute.
Ecocide is not yet a separate core crime under the Rome Statute.
India has a law criminalising ecocide.
Chile and Vietnam are the only countries with ecocide laws.
q.x: Ecocide is not a separate ICC crime; India has no ecocide law, and Russia, Ukraine, France and Belgium also have such laws.

q.s: CHOGM 2026, on whose sidelines S. Jaishankar met Guyana's President, was held in:
q.x: CHOGM 2026 was held in Antigua and Barbuda; Samoa hosted CHOGM 2024.

q.s: Which of the following Indian States does NOT share a border with Myanmar?
q.x: The 1,643 km India-Myanmar border touches Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram; Tripura borders Bangladesh.

q.s: The Habshan-Fujairah oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, is located in:
q.x: The Habshan-Fujairah pipeline runs across the UAE to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman.

q.s: A trade arrangement in which members remove tariffs among themselves and also adopt a common external tariff is called a:
q.x: A Customs Union adds a common external tariff to an FTA; a Common Market adds free movement of capital and labour.

q.s: India's Indian Ports Global Limited signed a 10-year contract in May 2024 to operate a terminal at:
q.x: IPGL signed a 10-year contract for the Shahid Beheshti terminal, Chabahar, Iran.

q.s: Agalega, where India has developed a forward naval facility, belongs to:
q.x: Agalega islands belong to Mauritius.

q.s: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) works under the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
q.x: NPPA is under the Department of Pharmaceuticals; it capped trade margins on 137 anti-cancer medicines under DPCO 2013.

q.s: A Doppler Weather Radar detects rainfall and cyclones using:
q.x: DWRs use radio waves; X-band is for thunderstorms and C-band for rainfall and cyclone tracking.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: X-band radars are used mainly for tracking cyclones over the sea.
C-band Doppler radars are used mainly for rainfall and cyclone tracking.
Doppler radars measure wind speed using sound waves.
A Doppler radar updates its data only once a day.
q.x: C-band is for rainfall and cyclones, X-band for local thunderstorms; DWRs use radio waves and update about every 10 minutes.

q.s: 'Dharma Guardian' is a joint military exercise between India and:
q.x: Dharma Guardian is with Japan; Vajra Prahar is with the USA and Khanjar with Kyrgyzstan.

q.s: Which of the following exercise–partner pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: DOSTI is the trilateral coast guard exercise of India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

q.s: The Heron Mk II UAV used by the Indian forces is made by:
q.x: Heron Mk II is a MALE UAV built by Israel Aerospace Industries.
